status: predeclared next experiment; not implemented or launched in this diagnostic step
question: Does averaging regression loss per assigned object instead of per positive grid point improve small-device localization and fixed validation performance?

candidate.formula: For each image and GT object with >=1 actual assigned FCOS point: average GIoU over its assigned points; then average those object losses over the batch. Empty objects contribute no invented targets; zero-positive batch retains zero regression loss.
candidate.assignment_identity: Use actual target assignment object identity; never merge separate objects by class.
candidate.scope: Only regression term; classification/centerness formulas and weights stay unchanged. Default remains old behavior.

fixed.validation_selection: highest recall, earlier wins tie; report best andlast

checks_before_training: Overlap and same-class distinct-object assignment identities remain exact.
Equal points per object agrees with old regression loss; duplicating one object points does not increase its weight.
Unknown/unassigned positions and classification/centerness losses unchanged.
Zero-positive and CUDA mixed precision deterministic backward finite.
Control reproduces previous assigned model best/last and history.
risks: Equal object weighting can amplify uncertain tiny AI labels.
Train size correlation and supervision point counts do not prove causal underweighting.
No new image detail or finer feature grid is created by changing loss normalization.
Six-frame source validation reused; scores are not independent accuracy.
